results.1: The Pioneer. Believes anyone willing to work hard deserves the opportunity to establish a new life.
results.2: The Loyal Subject. Regards eastern expansion as a necessary means of restoring Cador’s prosperity.
results.3: The Fortune Seeker. Cares little for politics; the frontier is simply where fortunes are made.
results.4: The Frontiersman. Believes the people who settle the frontier should govern themselves.
results.5: The Traditionalist. Regards the East as an extension of Cador that must respect established noble authority.
results.6: The Reconciler. Believes settlers and the frontier’s established inhabitants can prosper through cooperation.
results.7: The Dispossessed. Has come east because there was nothing left for them elsewhere.
results.8: The Land Speculator. Sees the frontier primarily as a source of investment and personal enrichment.
results.9: The Protector. Believes expansion must respect the rights and territories of existing peoples.
results.10: The Supremacist. Regards Cadorian civilization as inherently superior to the societies of the wilderness.
results.11: The Cynic. Believes the marquises and merchant companies will eventually exploit the frontier’s commonfolk just as their predecessors did.
results.12: The Escapist. Came east to escape the influence of kings, nobles, guilds, and political conflicts altogether.
